articles.title: An Ode to the Endeavour Space Shuttle
articles.summary: I’m standing on the floor of the Samuel Oschin Air and Space Center of the California Science Center under the tail of the new exhibit of the Space Shuttle Endeavour and remembering how I felt looking up at that same shuttle on the launch pad at the Kennedy Space Center in Florida. There is no one word to describe that feeling: wonder, awe, amazement, immense pride that we could build and fly such a machine. How was this my job, I think to myself. articles.title: How the War Turned Sudan Into a Country Without a Newspaper
articles.summary: A war of narratives is being waged within the war in Sudan. The warring parties—the official Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), a paramilitary force—are fighting an information war through traditional and social media. Misinformation, disinformation, hate speech, and propaganda are routinely deployed, and Sudanese journalists have become targets. articles.title: Big Tech Companies May Face Billion-Dollar Fines After Australia Passes ‘Digital Duty of Care’ Law
articles.summary: Tech giants could face penalties of up to 5% of their global revenue if found in violation of new online safety rules in Australia. The country’s Parliament passed the Digital Duty of Care bill Wednesday, Communications Minister Anika Wells said , after the center-left Labor Party government of Prime Minister Anthony Albanese reached a deal with the left-wing Greens party. articles.title: China’s Huawei Convicted in U.S. Over Bank Fraud, Iran Ties
articles.summary: China’s biggest technology firm and the world’s largest telecommunications equipment maker has been convicted in the U.S. of stealing trade secrets and defrauding banks about its business in Iran. Huawei was found guilty on 10 of 12 counts by a jury in Brooklyn on Tuesday. The verdict all but brings to a close an almost eight-year-long criminal case against Huawei and three of its subsidiaries.
